<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba244f1b487ffdf036c1b239757656801144cffe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3aeea260f65650ba3964fd03d4116beabc422d4c` — the merge of head `b5445185ddd2dad21abda0696bd295ee55a20166` into base `ba244f1b487ffdf036c1b239757656801144cffe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3aeea260f65650ba3964fd03d4116beabc422d4c && git checkout 3aeea260f65650ba3964fd03d4116beabc422d4c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ba244f1b487ffdf036c1b239757656801144cffe b5445185ddd2dad21abda0696bd295ee55a20166 && git checkout -B drift-repro ba244f1b487ffdf036c1b239757656801144cffe && git merge --no-ff b5445185ddd2dad21abda0696bd295ee55a20166

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba244f1b487ffdf036c1b239757656801144cffe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ba244f1b487ffdf036c1b239757656801144cffe` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b5445185ddd2dad21abda0696bd295ee55a20166`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-ui.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-platform-managed.pin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-auth-gate.pin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-setup-access.pin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/error-envelope.conformance.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-installed-ui-entry.pin.test.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup.app.ts (`SETUP_APP`: `group_apps` :60–65 ungated, `group_integrations` :104–109 `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']`, app-level `setup.access` :47), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`filterNav` :1014–1018 and :1103–1105), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (:183–196, the `organization_admin` grant set) and packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts (`ORGANIZATION_ADMIN_GRANTS`), packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-outbox-plugin.ts (:255–256), packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts (:573–574), packages/mcp/src/connect-ui.ts (:14–42 and :103–104), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (:95, :189) and packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (:56–70), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (:52–54, :1493–1499), docs/adr/0112-error-code-vocabulary-and-ledger.md (D2, D3), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (:58–96, :828), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (:131–154), AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3), the 19 other pending `.changeset/*.md` carrying `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, and the four prose faces (`.changeset/25097-cloud-connection-platform-managed.md`, `content/docs/deployment/cloud-connection.mdx`, `content/docs/ui/setup-app.mdx`, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json`) judged in ②.

### ① Derived judgments

**Check-runs on the head.** Read twice (the 11:55Z batch, and again at record time): 31 `success`, 6 `skipped` (opt-in and matrix-placeholder jobs), and 4 still `in_progress` at record time — Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6). Those four are NOT MEASURED; this record judges on the diff. Every completed gate is green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, every Lint and Type Check job, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core (5/6) and (6/6), Spec property liveness, the claim and single-writer guards. The Tier S landing waits on the four shards whatever this verdict says.

**Net diff.** Merge-base `5050442bb`; `origin/main` has since advanced to `ba244f1b` and touches none of the 11 files, nor `setup.app.ts`, so the diff reads the same against current main. 11 files, +608 / −57. No exported declaration added, removed or re-typed: `index.ts` is untouched, `PLATFORM_MANAGED_UNBIND_REFUSAL` is a module-private `const`, and the plugin's three exports are unchanged.

1. **`credential()` — RIGHT, behaviour-identical on every runtime.** Before: `cloudApiKey || this.store.read()?.runtimeToken || ''`. After: `platformManaged ? cloudApiKey : this.store.read()?.runtimeToken || ''` with `platformManaged = cloudApiKey !== ''` and `cloudApiKey` already trimmed at :304. Key non-empty: both arms return the key. Key empty: both arms return the stored token or `''`. The store read stays inside the closure, per call, so a runtime without the key that completes a device bind while up presents the new `oscc_` token on the next request exactly as before. A runtime with the key never presented the stored token before either; nothing moves there.

2. **Registration — RIGHT, ruling 甲 row 1.** `manifest.register(CLOUD_CONNECTION_UI_BUNDLE)` now sits in the `else` of `if (platformManaged)` (:400–411); the managed arm logs one `info` line. The predicate is read once at `kernel:ready`, at the same point `cloudApiKey` has always been resolved, so a page cannot register for a key set later — matching the comment's claim. No page, no `nav_cloud_connection`, on a keyed runtime.

3. **The 409's position — RIGHT on every path.** The unbind handler (:819–872) is one linear sequence with no branch before the refusal: 404 `ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND` (multi-env without an id) → held-session 403 → 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` → `holdsSetupAccess` 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (an `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` re-raises to the host's 503, the pre-existing outage path) → `if (platformManaged)` 409 → revoke fetch → store write or clear. Neither the revoke nor the store is reachable before the 409, and a caller without a session or without `setup.access` learns nothing about how the credential is held. The managed-shape CONTROL in the setup-access pin runs the 403 cases on the keyed mount, so the 403-before-409 ordering is pinned, not only read.

4. **Error code — RIGHT.** `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` is the standard catalog's 409 member (`errors.zod.ts` :95, :189). The ledger's own rule ("Registering a new code", `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` :56–70, mechanical since #8211) sends a generic condition to the standard catalog rather than a registered synonym; a minted code would need a `packages/spec` ledger entry the dispatch held off. The precedent cited is real: the install-local door answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` for a refusal that comes from runtime state (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` :52–54, :1495). The envelope is pinned against `BaseResponseSchema`, `envelopeViolations` and `ApiErrorSchema` in the new pin and in `error-envelope.conformance.test.ts`.

5. **Status route — RIGHT, unchanged.** No hunk touches :587–636. The served shape is still `{ bound, runtimeId, provider }` for a caller without `setup.access` and the full record otherwise; `bound` is still `Boolean(credential())`, which item 1 shows unchanged. No `managed` field. The claim's hold-off is honoured.

6. **Nav move — RIGHT, ruling 甲 row 2.** `CLOUD_CONNECTION_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS[0].group` moves `'group_apps'` → `'group_integrations'`, priority 200 kept; the item and its type are unchanged. The other contributors read where declared: webhooks 100, datasources 100, connect-agent 110, so 200 sorts last, as the ui.ts comment states. One exported constant's value changes (and `CLOUD_CONNECTION_UI_BUNDLE` carries it); its type does not.

7. **The nav move's permission consequence — RIGHT as read, implied by the placement, two rules remain, not a block.** Measured in the cited code: `SETUP_APP.group_integrations` declares `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']` (`setup.app.ts` :108) while `group_apps` declares none (:60–65); `filterNav` (`meta-item-read-gate.ts` :1017) drops a group entry whose `requiredPermissions` the caller lacks, children included, server-side, so the entry is not SERVED to such a caller, not merely hidden; and `organization_admin` holds `setup.access`, `setup.write`, `manage_org_users` and deliberately not `manage_platform_settings` (`security-plugin.ts` :183–196). So on a runtime without the key an organization administrator who could open the entry from `group_apps` no longer receives it. Judgments: (a) it is a consequence the ruling's placement implies — the ruling named the group, the gate is that group's own declared, pre-existing property, it already applies to every sibling entry (webhooks, datasources, connect-agent), and `packages/mcp/src/connect-ui.ts` :25–34 records that the app-level `setup.access` gate and the group gate were measured together once before and kept — it is not a defect the diff introduced; (b) yes, it leaves two rules for one capability: the entry is served on `manage_platform_settings`, while the three doors (`bind/start`, `bind/poll`, `unbind`) and the page itself (`cloud_connection_settings` carries no `requiredPermissions` of its own and is reachable by URL) take `setup.access` alone; the narrowing runs in the safe direction (fewer see, nobody new may act, the doors are unchanged), it is declared `no (narrowing)`, it is row 5 of the PR's Contract table and a sentence in the changeset and in `cloud-connection.mdx`; (c) it does not block — it belongs to the maintainer as a question (③ item 2). One nit, not a block: the plugin's #24148 header (:45–59, "the three doors ... refuse exactly who that page refuses") still holds for the page and no longer for the entry; `cloud-connection-ui.ts` :70–71 records the group gate, the plugin header does not.

8. **Existing pins — RIGHT, none loosened.** `cloud-connection-auth-gate.pin.test.ts`: `mountCloudConnection` gains a `serviceKey` parameter defaulting to the key, so every HELD case still runs on the shape it always ran on; the UN-HELD control splits into self-hosted (all seven doors 200, unbind driven last because it really clears the credential) and managed (six doors 200, unbind 409 with no control-plane call). `cloud-connection-setup-access.pin.test.ts`: the CONTROL likewise reads both shapes; bind start and bind poll keep every prior assertion in both; the 403 refusals still run on the keyed mount. `marketplace-installed-ui-entry.pin.test.ts`: the `group_apps` control switches to `nav_marketplace_browse` with `MARKETPLACE_BROWSE_UI_BUNDLE` registered in the composition, and the shell gains the `group_integrations` anchor; the page-listing control is unchanged. `error-envelope.conformance.test.ts`: the 409 case is added beside the others. A `''` key is `'' ?? env` — not nullish — so the env spelling is not consulted, as both fixtures' comments say.

9. **New pin — RIGHT.** 8 cases. Registration is read back through a real `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` metadata protocol with lit controls in the same composition (`control_settings` served, `nav_marketplace_browse` in `group_apps`), under both spellings of the key (`controlPlaneApiKey: undefined` falls through `??` to `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY`), plus the not-managed reading pinning the entry as the only child of `group_integrations`, absent from `group_apps`, once in the tree. The boot line is pinned to exactly one. Unbind is driven in both resolution modes: managed 409 in the declared envelope, message's first sentence pinned, zero control-plane calls, stored credential untouched; control 200 with exactly one revoke call and the credential cleared. The unfiltered protocol read pins registration, not the group gate; that gate is `filterNav`'s and is pinned there, which is the right layer. No read escapes the package.

10. **Named pins left unmodified — reasons read right.** `platform-page-i18n-parity.test.ts` reads the static bundle's pages, and the page is unchanged; `check-app-nav-i18n.mjs` keys labels by app and nav id (`apps.setup.navigation.nav_cloud_connection`), which the regroup does not touch; `platform-app-object-entry-views.test.ts` judges `type: 'object'` entries and this one is `type: 'page'`. The claim asked that they be updated, not loosened; an update with nothing to update is the honest reading. Their CI shards are among the four not yet measured.

11. **Docs — consistent with the behaviour.** `cloud-connection.mdx`: the Setup path, a managed-server paragraph (no page, no entry, one boot line, 409 with nothing revoked or cleared), the group-gate sentence that records the two-rule state plainly, and the reference row for the disconnect request. `setup-app.mdx`: the Apps and Integrations rows. `platform-core.json`: `platform-core.marketplace-console-honesty` steps[3] and acceptance[0] re-pointed, revision 6 with a history entry; the item's ownership rule is unchanged.

12. **Bind/start and bind/poll on a managed runtime — unchanged, and correctly out of scope.** Both doors still run and bind/poll still writes a device credential that `credential()` never presents while the key is set (the managed CONTROL in the setup-access pin shows `oscc_new` persisted, then the refused unbind leaving it in place). That shape is main's today (the old `credential()` preferred the key too) and the card holds the binding flow off. Escalated in ③, not a block.

### ② Semver level

The diff publishes from `@objectstack/cloud-connection` (`18.0.0`, not private). What changes is served behaviour: a keyed runtime refuses a disconnect it carried out and no longer registers the page or entry; a key-less runtime serves the entry in a gated group. Nothing widens — no new key on any published payload (the status shape is unchanged, the 409 rides the declared envelope, the boot line is a log), no new export, no removed export. So `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right line, on the PR body and in the changeset, and the review face is the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.

**Level: `minor` is right; the card's `patch` is not.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: "`(narrowing)` is BREAKING". `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (:58, :79, :828) records the launch-window convention under which a breaking change ships as `minor`, and refuses `major`. All 20 pending changesets carrying `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, this one included, grade their primary package `minor`. A `patch` would have declared a narrowing non-breaking against the rule file that wins over the card. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner and the adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` in the comment form the gate reads; the category is honest — the body carries no rewrite instruction (the "Nothing to rewrite" bullet is a statement, not a prescription), nothing authorable moves, and the only exported change is a value inside a constant of unchanged type. Check Changeset is `success` on the head. The changeset describes behaviour only, in keeping with the #9387 discipline the card names.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's report is comment 6315317491 on #25097: eight deviations, two out-of-scope findings, no open questions.

1. **Changeset level `minor` versus the card's `patch` — answered: `minor`, per ②.**

2. **Nav-permission consequence (entry served on `manage_platform_settings`, doors on `setup.access`) — answered in ① item 7; escalated to the maintainer as a question, not a block.** The question for the maintainer: ruling 甲 placed the entry in Integrations for prominence; its group gate means a `setup.access`-only administrator (the default `organization_admin` set) on a self-hosted runtime no longer sees the entry yet may still open the page by URL and drive connect and disconnect. Should the three doors and the page follow the group's `manage_platform_settings` so one rule governs the capability, or should the entry stay exactly where the ruling put it with the split recorded, as this PR does? Either answer is a new ruling; this PR's declared narrowing stands on its own.

3. **File surface beyond the claim (auth-gate and setup-access pins, the envelope conformance test, three docs, the changeset) — answered: each is a file the behaviour change falsified or the dispatch's convention pointer named; none drops a prior assertion.** The request to amend the claim's file surface is the seat's act.

4. **Named pins needing no edit — answered: ① item 10.**

5. **`RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with no minted code — answered: ① item 4.**

6. **Attribution — not a contract matter.** All four commits carry the model-free trailer pair AGENTS.md prescribes; no model identifier in the trailers, the PR body or the changeset.

7. **A stopped lint run of the dev's own — not a contract matter;** the ESLint job on the head is `success`.

8. **#9387 discipline — answered: the PR body's Contract table describes answers and effects, no request shapes.**

Out-of-scope finding 1 — **bind/start and bind/poll on a managed runtime — escalated as a follow-up card for the lane seat, not a block.** It is the symmetric half of what this card fixed: a hand-driven bind on a keyed runtime presents the service key to the control plane's `/bind` and persists a local credential the key shadows, so the cloud-side row and the local store can be moved by a door the runtime cannot act on. The dev's "zero pull" reading holds only while nothing in the product reaches those doors, and they are public routes. The ruling's table carries one Unbind column and the card names the binding flow out of scope, so this PR is right not to touch them; Prime Directive #10 makes a reproducible defect card material rather than an acceptance note, so the carrier should be a card, not "none".
